title: Afghanistan vs India T20Is: Full Schedule, Squads and How to Watch
excerpt: Three T20 internationals at Delhi's Arun Jaitley Stadium on September 13, 15 and 17 — Afghanistan's first series as host against India, with Jasprit Bumrah back in India's squad.
body:
• Afghanistan faces India in a three-match T20I series on September 13, 15 and 17, 2026, with every game starting at 7:00 p.m. IST at Delhi's Arun Jaitley Stadium.
  • Afghanistan is the designated host for the series — the first time it will host a bilateral against India — even though all matches are played in New Delhi.
  • India's squad, led by Shreyas Iyer, includes a returning Jasprit Bumrah; Yash Thakur replaced the injured Harshit Rana on September 10.
  • Afghanistan is led by Ibrahim Zadran in his first series as full-time T20I captain, with Rashid Khan, Mohammad Nabi, Naveen-ul-Haq and Mujeeb Ur Rahman in the squad. TV coverage is on Sony Sports; streaming on FanCode.

The first ball of a historic three-match T20I series between Afghanistan and India will be bowled at Delhi's Arun Jaitley Stadium on Sunday, September 13, 2026. All three games start at 7:00 p.m. IST, with the second and third fixtures on September 15 and September 17. The series carries a unique status: Afghanistan is the designated host of a bilateral against India for the first time, even though every match is played in New Delhi.

For fans, this page collects the full schedule, both squads, broadcast details and the context around the series — including a late injury change to India's pace attack confirmed on September 10.

Full schedule

The series runs September 13–17, 2026, with all three fixtures at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi. That is 7:00 p.m. IST, 2:30 p.m. in the UK, and 9:30 a.m. ET for viewers in North America.

  • 1st T20I: Sunday, September 13 — Arun Jaitley Stadium, Delhi
  • 2nd T20I: Tuesday, September 15 — Arun Jaitley Stadium, Delhi
  • 3rd T20I: Thursday, September 17 — Arun Jaitley Stadium, Delhi

The Afghanistan Cricket Board formally confirmed the dates in a letter from CEO Naseeb Khan to board stakeholders and commercial partners, reported via Cricbuzz.

India squad: Bumrah back, late change in pace attack

India are led by Shreyas Iyer, with Tilak Varma as vice-captain. The headline selection is the return of Jasprit Bumrah to T20I cricket, alongside Arshdeep Singh leading the pace attack. Sanju Samson returns to the side after missing the Zimbabwe tour, giving India two wicketkeeping options with Ishan Kishan.

Full India squad: Shreyas Iyer (C), Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Sanju Samson (WK), Ishan Kishan (WK), Tilak Varma (VC), Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi, Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh, Yash Thakur.

The last change came on September 10, when Harshit Rana was ruled out with a strain injury and replaced by Yash Thakur. Several picks remain subject to fitness clearance, and Hardik Pandya remains out of international cricket with injury concerns.

Afghanistan squad: new captain, familiar firepower

Ibrahim Zadran leads Afghanistan as full-time T20I captain for the first time. The squad blends veteran names with returning players: fast bowler Naveen-ul-Haq is back after a shoulder injury, experienced all-rounder Gulbadin Naib has returned, and uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Noor Rahman has earned his first place in the squad.

Full Afghanistan squad: Ibrahim Zadran (C), Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Noor Rahman (WK), Sediqullah Atal, Darwish Rasooli, Azmatullah Omarzai, Gulbadin Naib, Mohammad Nabi, Rashid Khan, Nangyal Kharoti, Noor Ahmad, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Fazalhaq Farooqi, Abdullah Ahmadzai, Naveen-ul-Haq.

The spin trio of Rashid Khan, Mujeeb Ur Rahman and Noor Ahmad gives Afghanistan its familiar weapon against an Indian batting order stacked with power hitters.

How to watch

In India, the series airs on Sony Sports television channels and streams live on FanCode. Matches begin at 7:00 p.m. IST each match day. Diaspora viewers in the UK can follow from 2:30 p.m., and North American viewers from 9:30 a.m. ET.

Why Afghanistan is hosting in Delhi

Because ongoing geopolitical issues prevent Afghanistan from staging regular home fixtures, the ACB has designated New Delhi as its temporary home venue through an arrangement with the BCCI and the Delhi and District Cricket Association. The T20I leg forms part of Afghanistan's multi-format bilateral cycle in India. The series also doubles as preparation for both sides ahead of the Asian Games, scheduled to begin in late September.

For the diaspora

The series sits at the intersection of two of cricket's most followed fan bases. Indian and Afghan diaspora communities — large in the UK, North America and the Gulf — follow these fixtures closely, and morning start times in North America make the games watchable before the workday. The novelty of Afghanistan officially hosting India adds an extra layer of interest beyond the on-field contest.

What's next

After the third T20I on September 17, both squads turn toward the Asian Games. For India, the series is a live audition under Shreyas Iyer's captaincy with Bumrah back in the side; for Afghanistan, it is the first test of the Ibrahim Zadran captaincy era.
